examples.name: Default
examples.summary: `LogViewer.Header` + `LogViewer.Content` over a realistic deploy log. Search filters lines and highlights matches in the body; with no `levels` set, the header offers the `warn` toggle alone, with its count, while the log has a warning.

examples.name: Borderless
examples.summary: With `:bordered="false"` the shell drops its own outline and corner radius so it sits flush inside a surface that already frames it — an accordion panel, a drawer, a card. Internal dividers (the header and footer edges) are unaffected. Left on, the two frames would nest and read as a box inside a box.

examples.name: Loading
examples.summary: While `loading` is set, `LogViewer.Content` replaces the log body with a centered spinner and the `loadingLabel` text.

examples.name: Levels
examples.summary: A function's test-run log: each line has a `level` and its run offset in `time`, and `levels` on the root puts one toggle per level in the header with the count of lines at that level. Pressing a toggle filters the log to that level (`v-model:level`), pressing it again shows every level. The line count and the toggles share one size and font, and on a phone the strip scrolls sideways instead of wrapping; `warn` and `error` rows are tinted and keep the level in text.

examples.name: Empty
examples.summary: A log with no lines shows the package empty state ("No log lines yet."). A search that matches nothing shows "No line matches …" with a Clear search action instead.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.summary: `disabled` keeps the lines readable but locks the search, the level toggles and the copy control.

examples.name: WithFooter
examples.summary: `LogViewer.Footer` closes the shell with a summary line and an action, below the scrolling body.

examples.name: StepLogs
examples.summary: Still `LogViewer`, not a separate component: a deploy log split into its steps with `LogViewer.Steps`, the way GitHub Actions, Vercel and Netlify show a run. Each step is a collapsible row with its status and its own log (Phased), or every line in one log (Complete). The `header` slot holds the title, the outcome and the time; `open-step` opens Build. For a wizard's progress use `Stepper`, for request spans use `Trace`.

examples.name: StepLogsRunning
examples.summary: The same step logs mid-run: done steps, the running step with its spinner and shimmering description, pending steps waiting to start, and `progress` drawing the flush bar valued by the share of steps done. `:view-switch="false"` keeps the Phased/Complete switch out until the run settles.

examples.name: StepLogsError
examples.summary: The same step logs after a failure: the failed step opens on its own with the reason in danger text, the step after it is skipped, `#step-meta` adds a Skipped `Tag` and `#step-empty` says why it never ran.
